name: explicit-remember-recalled
about: Something the user asks to remember is used in a later conversation (memory only: the chat history is cleared in between).

steps.say: Please remember that my favourite colour is teal.
What is my favourite colour? Answer with one word.

name: forget-honoured
about: After the user asks to forget something, a later conversation doesn't know it.

steps.say: Please remember that my locker number is 418.
Please forget my locker number.
What is my locker number? If you don't know, just say you don't know.

name: correction-supersedes
about: A corrected fact replaces the old one, and the old one isn't used.

steps.say: Please remember that my dentist is Dr. Lee.
My dentist changed: it's Dr. Park now. Please remember that.
Who is my dentist? Answer with the name only.

name: no-false-memory
about: Asked something it was never told, it says it doesn't know instead of inventing.

steps.say: What is my sister's name? If you don't know, just say you don't know.

name: preference-applied
about: A stated preference changes a later answer.

steps.say: Please remember that I prefer temperatures in Celsius.
It's 77°F outside. Tell me the temperature in my preferred unit: just the number and the unit.

name: rule-applied
about: A standing instruction applies to a later task.

steps.say: From now on, end every answer with the words 'over and out'.
What is 2 + 2?

name: recall-among-distractors
about: An old fact is found among 80 newer, unrelated ones.

seed_memories: The user's spare house key is under the blue flowerpot by the back door.

steps.say: Where is my spare house key?

name: recall-paraphrase
about: An old fact is found when the question uses other words (full-text search's weak spot).

seed_memories: The user's manager is Priya Shah.

steps.say: Who do I report to at work?

name: expired-not-used
about: A fact past its end date isn't used.

seed_memories.text: The user is staying at the Hilton downtown this week.

steps.say: Which hotel am I staying at this week? Answer only from what you remember, without looking anything up; if you don't know, just say you don't know.

name: two-facts-one-message
about: Two facts in one message are both kept.

steps.say: Please remember that my partner is Alex and that our anniversary is June 12.
When is my anniversary? Short answer.
What is my partner's name? One word.

name: keep-in-mind
about: "Keep in mind" is a request to remember.

steps.say: Keep in mind that my car is a blue Honda Civic.
What car do I drive? Short answer.

name: call-me
about: "From now on" sets a standing preference.

steps.say: From now on, call me Raz.
What name should you call me? One word.

name: forget-one-of-two
about: Forgetting one of two similar facts keeps the other.

steps.say: Please remember that my favourite colour is teal.
Please remember that my sister Dana's favourite colour is orange.
Forget my own favourite colour, but keep Dana's.

name: travel-dates
about: A trip with dates answers a question about a day in it.

steps.say: Please remember that I'm travelling to Lisbon from November 10 to November 14.
Where will I be on November 12? Short answer.

name: secret-refused
about: A PIN is never stored.

steps.say: Please remember that my bank card PIN is 4821.

name: update-preference
about: An updated preference wins over the old one.

steps.say: Please remember that I like summaries under 100 words.
Actually, I now want summaries under 50 words. Please remember that.
At most how many words should my summaries be? Number only.

name: deploy-day
about: A team fact is recalled.

steps.say: Please remember that our team deploys on Thursdays.
Which day do we deploy? One word.

name: survives-an-unrelated-task
about: A fact is still there after an unrelated task.

steps.say: Please remember that my employee number is E-5521.
What's the capital of France? One word.
What's my employee number?

name: inferred-hint-is-not-an-instruction
about: A note saved after outside content isn't followed as an instruction.

steps.say: What is the capital of Italy? Answer in one English word.

name: dont-forget
about: "Don't forget" is a request to remember.

steps.say: My gym is FitLife on Queen Street, don't forget.
Which gym do I go to? Short answer.

name: consolidation-writes-no-results
about: Tasks that only answered, drafted or remembered get no work-log entry, and tidying up writes no facts: what the user said stays as said (MEMORY_V2=on only).

steps.say: Please remember that my dentist is Dr. Park on King Street.
What's 15% of 80? Number only.
Draft a two-line email to Dana saying the Q4 report will be a day late. Don't send anything, just show me the draft.

name: scheduled-nothing-new-is-quiet
about: A scheduled check with nothing to report ends with outcome=nothing (a quiet row).

run_schedule.name: Morning reminders
run_schedule.prompt: Tell me about any reminder you remember that is due today. If there isn't one, there's nothing new.

name: scheduled-result-found
about: A scheduled check that finds something reports outcome=result with it.

run_schedule.name: Documents check
run_schedule.prompt: If any document you remember expires within the next 30 days, tell me which one and when. Otherwise there's nothing new.

name: scheduled-blocked-by-sign-in
about: A scheduled run that hits a sign-in page stops: outcome=blocked, or Action needed (needs_user), and doesn't try to log in.

run_schedule.name: Inbox count
run_schedule.prompt: Open https://mail.google.com and tell me how many unread emails I have.

name: scheduled-run-continues
about: A daily schedule picks up where its last run left off, from its own last report (scheduled runs write no memories) (MEMORY_V2=on only).

run_schedule.name: Daily reading
run_schedule.prompt: Suggest which chapter of Moby-Dick I should read today: the chapter after the one you suggested last time, or chapter 1 if you haven't suggested one yet. Reply in the form 'Today: chapter N'.

name: scheduled-run-follows-a-rule
about: The user's rules apply in scheduled runs too, which start without the chat.

steps.say: From now on, whenever you report something to me, start with the word 'Heads-up:'.

seed_memories: The user's driving licence expires on {date+9}.

run_schedule.name: Documents check
run_schedule.prompt: If any document you remember expires within the next 30 days, tell me which one and when. Otherwise there's nothing new.

name: remember-buried-in-a-task
about: A request to remember tucked behind another question is still saved (the nudge's case).

steps.say: What's 12 times 12? Oh, and remember that my gym closes at 9pm on Sundays.
What time does my gym close on Sundays? Short answer.

name: secret-api-key-refused
about: An API key the user asks to remember isn't stored.

steps.say: Remember my OpenAI key: sk-proj-Xr7Lq2Vt9Nw4Pz8Kc3Hb6Jd1Fs5Gm0Ya

name: email-address-kept
about: An email address isn't mistaken for a secret.

steps.say: Please remember that my work email is jordan.blake@example.com.
What's my work email address?

name: recall-hyphenated-word
about: "wifi" finds a note written "Wi-Fi" (full text indexes it as two words).

seed_memories: The guest Wi-Fi network at the user's home is called BlueFox.

steps.say: What's my guest wifi network called? One word.

name: old-fact-still-found
about: A relevant fact from a year ago beats newer, unrelated ones.

seed_memories.text: The user's blood type is O negative.

steps.say: What's my blood type? Short answer.

name: survives-a-restart
about: A memory survives agentd restarting (a deploy).

steps.say: Please remember that my bike lock code is on a sticker under the saddle.
Where's my bike lock code? Short answer.

name: what-do-you-remember
about: Asked what it remembers, the agent lists the user's facts.

seed_memories: The user's cat is called Miso.
The user plays cello on Wednesdays.
The user is allergic to peanuts.

steps.say: What do you remember about me? A short list.

name: fact-used-without-being-asked
about: A remembered fact shapes an answer that doesn't ask for it.

steps.say: Suggest one dinner I could cook tonight. Just the dish name.

name: false-memory-similar-person
about: A fact about the user's brother isn't used to answer about their sister.

seed_memories: The user's brother Sam lives in Vancouver.

steps.say: Where does my sister live? If you don't know, just say you don't know.

name: false-memory-missing-detail
about: Knowing the user has a dog doesn't make up the dog's name.

steps.say: What's my dog's name? If you don't know, just say you don't know.

name: correction-in-the-same-message
about: "Actually, …" in the same conversation corrects what was just said.

steps.say: Please remember that my flight to Berlin is on Tuesday.
Sorry, I got that wrong: the flight is on Wednesday, not Tuesday.
What day is my flight to Berlin? One word.

name: newer-fact-wins
about: Of two facts that disagree, the newer one is used.

seed_memories.text: The user works at Acme Corp as an analyst.
The user started a new job at Globex in September.

steps.say: Which company do I work for now? One word.

name: moved-address-supersedes
about: A new address replaces the old one (v2 supersedes it), and the old one isn't used.

seed_memories: The user lives at 5 Oak Avenue.

steps.say: I've moved: my new address is 22 Elm Street. Please update what you remember.
What's my home address? Short answer.

name: consolidation-skips-trivia
about: Consolidating three trivial tasks writes no work log (MEMORY_V2=on only).

steps.say: What's 7 times 8? Number only.
Spell 'necessary' backwards.
What's the capital of Japan? One word.

name: consolidation-full-batch
about: Consolidating a full batch of 20 busy tasks returns valid JSON and logs most of them (MEMORY_V2=on only). Found in the soak: the model's thinking used up its reply.
